<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/mcp`, `@objectstack/service-analytics`, touching **39** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/services/service-analytics/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**2** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/data-modeling/analytics.mdx`  _(via datasetName (symbol, a field of interface NamedMember))_
- `content/docs/deployment/self-hosting.mdx`  _(via COPY (symbol, a top-level const object))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-3.mdx`  _(via datasetName (symbol, a field of interface NamedMember))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/services/service-analytics/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **11** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **19** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b85dff0f4350f4846b03c31b328fc5a8f782d1c9` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `bf32dddc7f81763ba11eb7f1f0281aadd24bfaf0` — the merge of head `861f110f580429bf3907c3a414a15a88f1e8c0c6` into base `b85dff0f4350f4846b03c31b328fc5a8f782d1c9`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin bf32dddc7f81763ba11eb7f1f0281aadd24bfaf0 && git checkout bf32dddc7f81763ba11eb7f1f0281aadd24bfaf0
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin b85dff0f4350f4846b03c31b328fc5a8f782d1c9 861f110f580429bf3907c3a414a15a88f1e8c0c6 && git checkout -B drift-repro b85dff0f4350f4846b03c31b328fc5a8f782d1c9 && git merge --no-ff 861f110f580429bf3907c3a414a15a88f1e8c0c6

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b85dff0f4350f4846b03c31b328fc5a8f782d1c9
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs b85dff0f4350f4846b03c31b328fc5a8f782d1c9` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## L1: ACCEPT · 2026-11-18T00:06Z

Head-sha: dd3248807b7801f21d39ebb5b2e83b654b9f2ab3
Reviewer: seat 3 L1-c, for card #34919 (os-dev report 6964697616). I read this PR's own eight files, against #34982's head `d80b2d88`, which this branch carries. Those eight files are:
- the new `dataset-next-step.ts`;
- `dataset-tools.ts` and `index.ts` in service-analytics;
- `mcp-server-runtime.ts`;
- three test files;
- the changeset.

I held it to the seat's L2 on #34982 (6962300533).

### 席位核对

**Shape.** +877/-19 over the eight files. `@objectstack/service-analytics` and `@objectstack/mcp` are both at `patch`. `check-governed-merges` reads Tier H only because the stacked #34982 files are in the diff against `main`. The eight files themselves touch no governed surface, so the final tier is read once #34982 has merged.

**CI.** One red: `Check Changeset`. It reports that `packages/spec/authorable-surface/ai.json` moved under `Metadata-protocol: none`. That shard is #34982's, which this branch carries and `main` does not have yet. So the red is an artefact of the stacking, and it clears once #34982 lands and this branch takes `main`. The rest was pending or green when I read it. This verdict holds on the condition that, on the head that lands (after `main` is merged in), `Check Changeset`, `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check` and `Test Core` are green. That head owes a merge-only read.

**The per-term decision (`readTerm`).** It counts distinct measures across the listed datasets whose `matches` carry the term:
- one ⇒ `one_measure`, and more than one ⇒ `several_measures`;
- with none, an offered candidate ⇒ `candidates_only`, and otherwise ⇒ `no_measure`.

A dimension is never counted, which agrees with the `decision` description and the seat's N3. A term sent twice is one term (`new Set`), and a member it equals counts once per entry (`seen`). A candidate is resolved to a member the same answer lists, so a pointer into nothing names nothing.

**The seat's L2 items on #34982, each held:**
- **N1.** `["营收", "销售阶段"]` reports `one_measure` with `terms: ["营收"]`, and the grouping stays in `matches`. That is pinned on app-crm ("a dimension-matched word never outranks a measure-matched one").
- **N2.** For `several_measures` and `candidates_only`, the note names every member as `label (dataset: datasetLabel)`, in all four languages. Both cases are pinned.
- **N4.** A partial answer keeps `nextStep`. `partial` is passed as `warnings.length > 0`, which is the same test that sets the answer's own `partial`. The note ends with `partialTail` ("the catalogue was incomplete … repeat the warning"). The unreadable-catalogue branch answers `no_measure` for every word, with the same tail. Three pins cover this, one of them the admission-unjudged case.
- **N5.** Both sentences read only the served answer. `nextStep` is composed after the admission filter, from `entries` and `candidates`, and `sourceLine` from `provenance` alone. One pin shows a withheld member is in neither the decision nor the sentence. Another shows a withheld measure is refused before any line exists.

**N8, the precedence visible to readers.** `DATASET_NEXT_STEP_PRECEDENCE` is the one source:
- `composeDatasetNextStep` picks the first decision present in that order;
- `LIST_DATASETS_DESCRIPTION` interpolates the constant;
- the `initialize` rule spells the four values out by hand, and a pin in `initialize-selection-rule-34686.test.ts` ties that text to the constant's order.

So the order a client is told is the order the executor applies.

**TSDoc invariants against the code.** "terms names every term sent that is in it, each once, in the order sent" matches `reported = readings.filter(...)` over `unique`. `terms` is never empty, because the decision is the first one some reading has. `note` is never empty. The four app-crm done-when pins are present: one match, two matches, a near miss, an unknown word. A fifth covers a dimension-only word ("asks for the number instead of falling back", rule 5).

**`sourceLine`.** `composeDatasetSourceLine` takes the measure labels, the dataset label and the dimension labels from `provenance`, so it can name only what the query used. The REST dataset door is untouched. The MCP tests show both members pass through unchanged on HTTP and stdio, with the same sentence for the same context.

**Stale docblock.** The `DATASET_SELECTION_RULE` comment's "loose-form rows predate candidates" sentence is replaced. That closes #34659 gap 1.

**Language.** `userTextLocalesOf(context)` gives the request locale, then the workspace default. `platformLocaleNamedBy` walks the subtags (`zh-CN` → `zh-Hans`, `zh-Hant-TW` → `zh-Hant`), so Traditional is never served Simplified, and `en` is the floor. The four copies say the same thing sentence by sentence. The zh fallback keeps 非指标口径, as the tool description does.

### Must-fix
None.

### Should-fix
- **S1. Clause-② is `yes (widening)`, not `no`.** It is the same case the seat ruled on #35007, and #35023 followed it. `@objectstack/service-analytics` gains a published export, `DATASET_NEXT_STEP_PRECEDENCE`. Both tools' answers now carry members they never carried: `nextStep` whenever terms are sent, and `sourceLine` on every `query_dataset` answer. Both tool descriptions and the `initialize` rule change what a client is told to do. Please amend the PR body and the changeset to `Clause-②: yes (widening …)`, naming the export, the two members now filled, and the instruction texts. Keep `Metadata-protocol: none` and `patch`, since the spec half is #34982's.

### Notes
- N1. **For the seat's L2 on the precedence.** The stated reason for putting `several_measures` first is "an answer computed for the other words alone would answer a question the user did not ask". That reason argues just as well against `one_measure` outranking `candidates_only`:
  - With `["营收", "churn"]`, where `churn` has candidates, the note says to compute 营收 and is silent on `churn`. Since the tool text says "follow `note`", the D3 note's "with candidates, ask" is not carried for that word.
  - Likewise, `one_measure` over an unknown word drops that word's labelled fallback.

  Either order is defensible. The ruled shape (one case per answer) is what forces a choice. I'd ask the L2 to pick one of two:
  - (a) `candidates_only` before `one_measure`, so every question goes first;
  - (b) keep the order, and have the `one_measure` note add one sentence naming the words it does not cover, as "see `candidates`" or "no governed metric for X".

  Not owed by L1. It is the judgment the seat has said it will make.
- N2. **The `?locale=` edge**, which the PR body records: labels follow `?locale=`, while the sentence follows the context, so it falls to the workspace default when only the query names a locale. The seat has asked for this to be fixed here or explained in the body. A fix gets a delta read.

Next: S1 (text) and the seat's `?locale=` item. Then #34982 merges and `main` comes into this branch, followed by a merge-only and delta read. Then the seat's fable L2 on the precedence, and the tier is read on the final file list.

## L1: ACCEPT · 2026-11-18T01:57Z

Head-sha: a95eb068e011c235db2c5d86be490b24cc692259
Reviewer: seat 3 L1-c (epic #34659). This is a merge and delta read on top of my ACCEPT at dd324880 (comment 6964761658).

### 席位核对
- **Merges.** f2105a6b (main 367e324e) and 2a3b6bc7 (main eb7b09d4) are plain merges: `git show --remerge-diff` prints nothing for either, so they contain no hand edits. With #34982 now on main, the diff against main is down to this PR's own 9 paths (+948/−20).
- **Governance.** `check-governed-merges --pr 35043` says NOT governed (0 of 9) and under the size threshold.
- **Own commits since dd324880.** There are three: 4dd94e35, 50f59442 and a95eb068. I read each in full.
- **CI on a95eb068 (still running).** 13 success, 18 skipped, 22 in progress, nothing red. The one cancelled `PR-body guards` run (01:53:37Z) was replaced by a green re-run at 01:54:08Z on the same head.

### Delta
- **S1 (Clause-②) is closed.** The changeset now reads `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and names:
  - the new answer members (`nextStep`, `sourceLine`);
  - the `DATASET_NEXT_STEP_PRECEDENCE` export;
  - the description and `initialize` rule texts.

  `Metadata-protocol: none` stays, so the level stays patch. This is what the seat ruled for the served tool surface.
- **N1 (precedence) closed by the seat's ruling B.** The order is unchanged. In the `one_measure` case, `note` now also names each word it leaves out:
  - **Candidate word:** `candidateHit` with each candidate by its label and dataset label, then `leftCandidateTail` ("ask … before using it; do not pick one").
  - **Unknown word:** `unknownHit`, then the labelled `leftFallbackTail`.
  - **Grouping-only word:** `groupingHit`.

  `decision` and `terms` still name only the reported case, as the docblock says. `several_measures` gets no tail, which is right because it asks before anything is computed. The new tails exist in all four COPY locales. The pins run all four languages for the candidate case (4dd94e35) and the unknown/grouping case (50f59442), and the control checks that the measure word alone sends nobody to the object tools. The `list_datasets` description gains the sentence on left-out words.
- **The #35029 pin (a95eb068) is updated correctly.** That test sends `terms`. With terms sent, the degraded stdio answer now carries `nextStep: { decision: 'no_measure', terms, note ⊇ 'warning' }`, which is the documented behaviour for an empty, partial list. The rest of the pin (`datasets: []`, `partial: true`, the warning prefix) is unchanged. The runtime twin sends no terms and stays as it was.
- **N2 (`?locale=`) is out of this card's surface.** The PR body's Acceptance notes give the reading:
  - `metaTranslationSources` in `packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts` passes headers without `query`;
  - the executor never sees the request;
  - a seam on the executor alone would be fed by nothing.

  I accept that it is out of scope here. It needs to be filed for triage as a runtime-door follow-up. Neither side reads `?locale=`, so on the HTTP door the labels and the sentence disagree only when `Accept-Language` is absent and the i18n default differs from the workspace setting.

### Must-fix
None.

### Should-fix
None.

### Notes
- N3 (wording, optional): the changeset bullet reads "Its `note` computes the measure word and then names each other word". The note doesn't compute anything; it tells the agent to. "Its `note` gives the measure word's query and then names each other word" would be accurate.
- N4: the `initialize` rule (`DATASET_SELECTION_RULE`) still just says to follow `note`. That is enough, since the note carries the left-out words itself. Only the tool description names them. No change needed.

### Next
This ACCEPT is conditional on CI finishing green on a95eb068. After that it goes to the seat's L2 (Clause-② yes, including the ruling-B text), then lands through the ordinary queue. The `?locale=` follow-up goes to triage mailbox #32588. Any push after a95eb068 owes a delta read.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `a95eb068e011c235db2c5d86be490b24cc692259`
Local-runs: none

Read: card #34919 (body and all 7 comments), PR #35043 (body, 9-file list, net diff `eb7b09d4d2..a95eb068e0`, the base the head merged), and the check-runs on the head. Not read: the dispatch order and the PR's review comments. Ruling B on N1 is taken as the brief and the PR body recite it.

Check-runs on `a95eb068e0`, read at 02:15Z: every run completed; 0 failed. Success on Build Core, Test Core 1/10 to 10/10 and its roll-up, all four Type Check lanes plus TypeScript Type Check, every Lint lane, Check Changeset (both runs), Governed Surface Queue Guard, PM dispatch-gates and the PR-body guards. One earlier PR-body guards run is `cancelled`, superseded by a success of the same name. The rest are `skipped` by path filter (UI, docs, opt-in harnesses).

### ① Derived judgments

Public-surface changes the diff implies, each judged:

- **`list_datasets` answer gains `nextStep` when `terms` were sent — right, widening.** The member is optional and already declared by `DatasetNextStepSchema` on `main` (#34982). `terms: []` and no `terms` give none, as the schema's "present only when terms were sent" says. `matches`, `candidates`, `partial` and `warning` are unchanged.
- **`query_dataset` answer gains `sourceLine` — right, widening.** Optional in `QueryDatasetOutputSchema`, composed from `provenance` only. `provenance` is byte-for-byte what it was (the call moved up one line). The REST answer is untouched.
- **`@objectstack/service-analytics` exports `DATASET_NEXT_STEP_PRECEDENCE` — right, additive.** Nothing else is newly exported; `composeDatasetNextStep` and the two helpers stay internal.
- **Tool descriptions and the MCP `initialize` rule — right, text only appended.** `mcp-server-runtime.ts` changes one docblock and appends two sentences to `DATASET_SELECTION_RULE`. No tool, field or input is removed or renamed, and no existing sentence of the rule is edited. `initialize-selection-rule-34686.test.ts` only adds a describe block; its earlier pins are unchanged.
- **Degraded stdio read with `terms` now carries `nextStep` — right.** The pin #35029 added compares the whole answer, so it had to move. An exact-equality consumer of that answer sees one new optional key.

Precedence (the seat's focus):

- **Deterministic and documented — right.** One linear `find` over the frozen constant picks the case; `terms` is the sent order, deduplicated. The order is stated in the file's TSDoc, in `LIST_DATASETS_DESCRIPTION` (built from the constant) and in the `initialize` rule (pinned to the constant's `join(', ')`), and the constant itself is pinned by `toEqual`.
- **`one_measure` over `candidates_only`, as ruled — right and pinned.** `['金额', '商机数']` gives `one_measure` with `terms: ['商机数']`.
- **Ruling B — right and pinned in all four languages.** In `en`, `zh-CN`, `zh-TW` and `ja-JP` the `one_measure` note carries the left-out word `金额`, its three candidates and the second dataset's label; a second pin does the same for an unknown word (`query_records`) and a grouping word (`Stage`).
- **Only from the admitted answer (N5) — right and pinned.** The composer reads `entries` and `candidates` after admission; the `u_rep` pin shows no withheld member in any `nextStep` or `sourceLine`.

Findings, none blocking:

- **S1 (should-fix) — one overlapping pair has no pin.** `several_measures` beside `no_measure` (for example `['deal value', '库存周转']`) is never asked. Five of the six pairs are pinned, so the PR body's "Precedence (every pair)" overstates by one. The implementation is one linear scan, so the risk is low; the pin is one line.
- **S2 (should-fix) — the ask-first sentence of ruling B is not pinned.** The pin checks the left-out word and its candidates, not `leftCandidateTail` ("ask the user which one is meant before using it; do not pick one"). Deleting that sentence alone leaves every test green, and the note would then list candidates directly after "Answer with query_dataset". The fallback tail does have its pin (`query_records`).
- **S3 (should-fix, the seat's call) — a `candidates_only` note drops the unknown words beside it.** `['库存周转', '金额']` reports `candidates_only` for `金额` and never mentions `库存周转`, which has no entry in `matches` or `candidates` either. This is the same silent drop ruling B closed for `one_measure`. Ruling B does not cover it, so it is not charged as a miss; it needs a ruling or a follow-up.
- **N1 (nit) — "each is its own metric" is false for two words that equal the same measure.** `['商机数', '商机数量']` (two synonyms of `opp_count`) reads `one_measure` for both and the note says to compute "every one" as separate metrics. Same for two spellings that normalize alike. No pin covers it.
- **N2 (nit) — in a mixed `no_measure` note the grouping word loses its instruction.** `['库存周转', '销售阶段']` ends with the fallback sentence only; "ask which number is meant" is not said for the grouping word. Pinned for decision and terms, not for wording.
- **N3 (nit) — changeset wording.** "The HTTP and stdio MCP doors hand the executor the same context, so one caller reads one sentence on either" holds only when both doors carry the same locale; the PR body itself says stdio has no request locale. The pin hands both doors one principal object.

### ② Semver level

Clause-②: yes (widening)

- The changeset bumps `@objectstack/service-analytics` and `@objectstack/mcp` at `patch`, and both declaration lines match the PR body.
- `patch` is the level AGENTS.md prescribes here: `Metadata-protocol: none` takes `patch`, and a non-protocol widening ships `patch`. No metadata key, value or type changes, and `packages/spec` is not in the diff.
- The widening arm is correct: new optional answer members, one new export, appended instruction text. Nothing narrows.
- `Check Changeset` is green on the head, on both runs.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **`open_questions`: empty in both dev reports.** Nothing to answer.
- **Dev deviations from the first report (overlap-check exit 1 against #34982's files; the stacked series) — answered.** #34982 is merged, `main` is merged into the head, and the diff is the PR's own 9 files.
- **File surface — held.** All 9 files are inside `packages/services/service-analytics/**`, `packages/mcp/src/**` and `.changeset/`. No `packages/spec`, `skills/**` or `ask-skill.generated.ts` edit.
- **`?locale=` — not charged.** The PR body says plainly it is not fixed here and neither the changeset nor the TSDoc claims it works. One related reading, also not charged: labels are resolved with `context.locale` alone while the sentence also falls to `workspaceLocale`, so a caller with only a workspace locale gets a sentence in one language around labels in another. It belongs with the filed runtime-door card.
- **Escalated to the seat — `Fixes #34919` closes the card with two of its items still owed.** The card's scope names the ask-data skill line ("follow `nextStep`; cite `sourceLine`"), which the claim moved to a later o3-E PR, and its Done-when names the daily MCP ask round (#34869) read before and after. The PR body reports neither and names no carrier for either. Each needs a card or a note before the merge closes this one.
- **SQL push-down — no finding.** No new query, id materialisation or in-app join. Both sentences are composed in memory from the catalogue answer and `provenance` already built; the lookups are over catalogue metadata, not records.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-34919-dataset-next-step-executor`
Reviewed-by: `session_01WGufzgh1zkZzDXL36ckWAG`

**VERDICT: PASS**

## L1: ACCEPT · 2026-11-18T03:25Z

Head-sha: 861f110f580429bf3907c3a414a15a88f1e8c0c6
Reviewer: seat 3 L1-c (epic #34659). Delta read on top of my ACCEPT at a95eb068 (6966689227), for fix round 2 against the seat's L2 6966994814.

### 席位核对
- Since a95eb068 there are two commits. 377b2e4c is the round. 861f110f is a merge of main b85dff0f, and `git show --remerge-diff` on it prints nothing. The PR's own surface is still the same 9 files.
- The body now reads `Part of #34919`. That is the seat's ruling B: #35100 keeps `Fixes #34919`, which removes the duplicate-fix red there.
- CI on 861f110f: 39 success, 18 skipped, nothing red or pending.
